source_refs.note: Exercise 6.5, Question 15 (book page 210); answer key PDF 308.

blocks.prompt: 15. Find the equations of the normals to the hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1\) which are parallel to the line \(2x - y = 5\).
blocks.explanation:
Normal woh line hai jo curve ke kisi point se guzre aur us point par tangent ke perpendicular ho.
"\(2x - y = 5\) ke parallel" ka matlab hai ke normal ka slope bhi 2 hona chahiye.
Rule kaunsa? Example 27 wala tareeqa: implicit differentiation se tangent ka slope, phir normal ka slope us ka negative reciprocal (ulta aur sign badla hua).
Plan: point \((x_1, y_1)\) par normal ka slope 2 ke barabar rakhenge aur dekhenge ke hyperbola par aisa point milta hai ya nahi.
Pehle se bata dein: is sawal mein ek dilchasp baat saamne aayegi, is liye har qadam dhyan se dekhiye.
steps:
Diya gaya: hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1\), aur normals line \(2x - y = 5\) ke parallel hon.
Maloom karna: aise normals ki equations.
Tareeqa: Example 27 mein point \((x_1, y_1)\) par tangent ka slope \(\frac{b^2 x_1}{a^2 y_1}\) aaya, is liye normal ka slope \(-\frac{a^2 y_1}{b^2 x_1}\) hai. Isay 2 ke barabar rakh kar hyperbola ki equation ke saath solve karenge; jo point mile us par normal likh denge.

\(a^2\), \(b^2\) aur zaroori slope parhein
\[a^2 = 9,\quad b^2 = 16\]
\[2x - y = 5 \Rightarrow y = 2x - 5\]
\[\text{Required slope} = 2\]
Kyun: Line ko \(y = mx + c\) shakal mein likha to \(x\) ka coefficient 2 slope hai. Parallel lines ke slopes barabar hote hain, is liye normal ka slope bhi 2 chahiye.

Point \((x_1, y_1)\) par normal ka slope
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{b^2 x}{a^2 y} = \dfrac{16x}{9y}\]
\[m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{9y_1}{16x_1}\]
Kyun: Example 27 ki tarah implicit differentiation se tangent ka slope \(\frac{16x_1}{9y_1}\) aaya. Normal tangent par perpendicular hai, is liye us ka slope tangent ke slope ka negative reciprocal hai: fraction ulat do aur sign badal do.
Dhyan dein: Normal ka slope \(-\frac{a^2 y_1}{b^2 x_1}\) hai; \(a^2\) aur \(b^2\) ki jagah badal dena aam ghalti hai.

Slope ko 2 ke barabar rakhein
\[-\dfrac{9y_1}{16x_1} = 2\]
\[y_1 = -\dfrac{32x_1}{9}\]
Kyun: Cross-multiply kiya: \(-9y_1 = 32x_1\), phir \(-9\) se divide kiya. Ab \(y_1\) ko \(x_1\) ki shakal mein likh liya taake hyperbola ki equation mein rakh sakein.

Point hyperbola par hona chahiye
\[\dfrac{x_1^2}{9} - \dfrac{1}{16}\cdot\dfrac{1024x_1^2}{81} = 1\]
\[\dfrac{x_1^2}{9} - \dfrac{64x_1^2}{81} = 1\]
\[\dfrac{9x_1^2 - 64x_1^2}{81} = 1\]
\[x_1^2 = -\dfrac{81}{55}\]
Kyun: \(y_1^2 = \frac{1024x_1^2}{81}\) rakha aur \(\frac{1024}{16} = 64\) kiya. Common denominator 81 le kar \(9 - 64 = -55\) aaya. Lekin kisi bhi real number ka square negative nahi ho sakta! Matlab hyperbola par aisa koi real point hai hi nahi jahan normal ka slope 2 ho.

Aisa kyun hota hai?
\[(x_1, y_1) = (3\sec\theta,\ 4\tan\theta)\]
\[m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{9(4\tan\theta)}{16(3\sec\theta)}\]
\[= -\dfrac{3}{4}\sin\theta\]
Kyun: Kitab ke parametric point \((a\sec\theta, b\tan\theta)\) se har point likha ja sakta hai. \(\frac{\tan\theta}{\sec\theta} = \sin\theta\) hota hai. Hyperbola par \(|\sin\theta| < 1\) rehta hai, is liye har normal ka slope \(-\frac{3}{4}\) aur \(\frac{3}{4}\) ke darmiyan hota hai. Seedhi baat: is hyperbola ke normals kabhi itne steep (seedhe khare) nahi ho sakte ke slope 2 ho.

Tasdeeq
\[-\dfrac{3}{4}\sin\theta = 2\]
\[\sin\theta = -\dfrac{8}{3}\]
\[\left|-\dfrac{8}{3}\right| > 1\;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Slope 2 ke liye \(\sin\theta = -\frac{8}{3}\) chahiye, lekin kisi bhi angle ka sine \(-1\) se chhota ya \(1\) se bara nahi hota. Dono raston (seedha substitution aur parametric shakal) ne ek hi baat batayi: is hyperbola ka koi normal slope 2 wala nahi. Is liye sahi jawab yeh hai ke aisa normal maujood hi nahi. Figure mein answer key wali lines bhi dekhiye: woh to curve ko chhooti hi nahi.
blocks.final_answer: Aisa koi normal maujood nahi: \(\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1\) ke har normal ka slope \(-\frac{3}{4}\sin\theta\) hai, jo \(-\frac{3}{4}\) aur \(\frac{3}{4}\) ke darmiyan rehta hai, is liye koi normal \(2x - y = 5\) (slope 2) ke parallel nahi.

answer_figure.alt: The hyperbola x squared over 9 minus y squared over 16 equals 1 with vertices (3, 0) and (minus 3, 0) and dashed asymptotes y equals plus or minus four thirds x; the two answer-key lines y equals 2x plus or minus 14 over 5 pass between the branches without touching the curve.
answer_figure.caption: Jawab ki figure: answer key wali lines y = 2x ± 14/5 hyperbola ko chhooti hi nahi, is liye normal nahi ho saktin (original drawing).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki answer key mein \(5y = 10x - 14\) aur \(5y = 10x + 14\) likha hai, yani \(y = 2x \mp \frac{14}{5}\). Yeh lines \(\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1\) ke normals nahi ho saktin, kyunke yeh hyperbola ko chhooti bhi nahi. Khud check kijiye: \(y = 2x + k\) ko \(16x^2 - 9y^2 = 144\) mein rakhein to \(20x^2 + 36kx + 9k^2 + 144 = 0\) banta hai, jis ka discriminant \(576(k^2 - 20)\) hai. \(k^2 = \frac{196}{25}\) jo 20 se chhota hai, is liye discriminant negative aur koi intersection nahi. Sahi jawab: is hyperbola ka koi normal \(2x - y = 5\) ke parallel nahi.
